newsitem.title: USA: Arkansas soybean plantings running ahead of normal.
newsitem.headline: Arkansas soybean plantings running ahead of normal.

text.p: Arkansas soybean planting was running ahead of normal as of Sunday, acccording to the state's weekly Agricultural Statistics Service update.
Soybeans were 72 percent planted up from 62 percent a week ago, 67 percent a year ago and 66 percent five year average. Fifty-nine percent emerged versus an average 53 percent.
Condition ratings were 70 percent in good to excellent catagories, 26 percent fair and four percent poor.
The report noted widespread rain and cool temperatures started the week with a drying trend and warm temperatures returned by mid-week.
Soil moisture supplies one percent very short, 25 percent short, 65 percent adequate and nine percent surplus.
Ten percent of soft red winter wheat was harvested, down from 21 percent a year ago and the 27 five-year average.
One hundred percent of the wheat was headed versus 100 percent a year ago and 98 percent average. In Monroe county, wheat yields were reported at 40-60 bushels, the report said.
Rice was 99 percent emerged, up from an average pace for the date of 97 percent. Condition ratings were 61 percent good to excellent, 35 percent fair and four percent poor.
"Rice flooding was reported by several districts," the report said.
